input.quote: 3.4 HDI's General Manager (as hereinafter defined), may upon no less than thirty (30) days prior written notice to the Company, have the right to inspect the records of the Company's General Manager reasonably related to the calculation of such payments during the Company's normal business hours. The fees incurred by HDI in connection with the inspection shall be borne by HDI.
input.rationale:
Section 3.4 is the only provision binding the Company to an audit/inspection right (no other audit, records or verification clause appears in the Agreement). It already satisfies two fallback elements on its material terms — inspections require no less than thirty (30) days' prior written notice (exceeding the 15-day floor) and HDI bears the inspection cost unconditionally (better than the "unless underpayment exceeds 10 percent" fallback) — and it is limited to payment-calculation records during normal business hours. However, it imposes no frequency limit, so HDI could inspect repeatedly, which fails the fallback's once-per-year element and edges into walk-away territory. We therefore propose the single minimal edit adding a once-per-year cap; we have not pursued the preferred independent-auditor, confidentiality, off-site and no-systems-access elements, since the fallback is the selected target and the existing notice and cost terms already sit at or above it.</parationale>
<parameter name="confidence">0.83

proposal.summary: Cap HDI's records inspection right at once per year in §3.4.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 3.4 gives HDI an unlimited number of inspections of our records; our playbook fallback requires audits to be limited to once per year. We have added that frequency cap and left the existing 30 days' notice, business-hours and HDI-borne cost terms untouched.
